QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_30

question.text: A fund has a beta of 0.7. If the market rises by 15%, what is the expected return of the fund?

explanation.text: The Logic: Beta measures the volatility of an equity investment relative to its index, with a market beta of 1; a beta of 0.7 means the fund is expected to move at 70% of the market's movement. Expected fund return = 0.7 x 15% = 10.50%. The Trap: Picking 15% ignores beta; 21.43% comes from dividing by beta instead of multiplying; 7% drops the 15% magnitude. Note: A beta below 1 indicates the fund is expected to move less than the index in both directions.
